source.section: Schedule SB (PDF page 1) and its Instructions: line 12 (SB Instructions PDF page 6; Publication 126 PDF pages 5-6 section 4.D); line 16 and its Caution (SB Instructions PDF page 7; Publication 126 PDF page 8 section 4.E(1); Publication 106 PDF page 4 section 3.C(1)); Form 1 lines 1-12 (Form 1 PDF page 1); Form 1 Instructions PDF page 15 line 8 and lines 10a-10b (PDF pages 15-16), PDF pages 35-37 2025 Standard Deduction Table (row named in worked), PDF page 15 line 12 with the PDF pages 38-43 Tax Table and PDF page 44 Tax Computation Worksheet; tax figured from the 2025 Tax Rate Schedules, Publication 106 PDF pages 6-7; Publication 126 PDF page 8: a distribution excluded under another provision, such as military retirement pay, is not in line 16

worked: Single, 68: military retirement pay 40,000, IRA distributions 30,000 and interest 30,000. Line 12 removes the military pay; line 16 takes only income not removed on lines 12-15, so its qualifying income is the IRA 30,000, capped at 24,000. Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = ira distribution (you) 30,000.00 + military pension paid by federal (you) 40,000.00 + interest 30,000.00 = 100,000.00. Federal taxable income = 100,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 = 82,250.00; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Form 1 line 1 federal AGI 100,000.00; line 2 Schedule I adjustments 0.00; line 3 100,000.00; line 4 additions 0.00; line 5 100,000.00. Schedule SB: line 12 military retirement pay = 40,000.00; line 16 retirement income subtraction: qualifying income you (age 68): IRA 30,000.00 = 30,000.00; smaller of 30,000.00 and the 24,000.00 cap = 24,000.00; line 50 total 64,000.00. Schedule SB line 17: federal AGI 100,000.00 is not less than 15,000.00, so no 5,000 subtraction. Form 1 line 6 64,000.00; line 7 Wisconsin income = 100,000.00 - 64,000.00 = 36,000.00. Line 8 standard deduction, 2025 Standard Deduction Table (Form 1 Instructions PDF page 35), row 36,000 to less than 36,500, column Single: 11,556.00 (printed row, at least / less than / single / joint / separate / head of household: 36,000 / 36,500 / 11,556 / 23,520 / 7,409 / 13,760). Line 9 = 36,000.00 - 11,556.00 = 24,444.00. Line 10a 1 x 700 = 700.00; line 10b 1 x 250 = 250.00; line 10c 950.00. Line 11 taxable income = 24,444.00 - 950.00 = 23,494.00. Line 12 tax, Schedule A (single) as numbers: 3.5% x 14,680.00 = 513.80 + 4.4% x 8,814.00 = 387.816; total 901.616, rounded once to 901.62. The Tax Table row 23,400 to 23,500 (PDF page 39) gives 900; expected keeps the schedule. Credits (lines 13-20, 30-35): none modelled; 0.00. State income tax 901.62.
accepted_approximations: The projection always takes the 24,000/48,000 subtraction for a person 67 or older, never the Wisconsin credits it bars (see not_modelled); a household whose credits are worth more would skip it.
